stories.title: Snowfall strands passengers, cargo at Khunjerab
summary: A GB police official told Dawn that snowfall was continuing at Khunjerab Top, leaving several vehicles and dozens of containers carrying imported goods from China stranded for hours.
In a press release, the GB police spokesperson said heavy snowfall was continuing from Dhee Headquarters to Khunjerab Top, while accumulated snow had made the road hazardous for travel.

In a video message, Minister Naiknaam Karim said snowfall had also occurred on the Chinese side, but the road had been cleared for traffic. “However, after entering the Pakistani side, we found the road at Khunjerab Top covered with approximately four inches of snow and ice.

stories.title: Fazl’s son skips another summons from NAB in Pakistan post case
summary: According to sources, the anti-graft watchdog will soon serve a third notice on the former minister and, in case he ignores it, NAB could take stern action, including his arrest.

Under the NAB notice, Asad Mehmood was req­uired to appear before the investigators to explain his position on alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments at Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 tenure as federal minister.
Asad Mehmood had served as a federal minister during the Pakistan Democratic Movement (PDM) government in 2022-23.Published in Dawn, November 14th, 2026

stories.title: Balochistan Assembly seeks compulsory Arabic in primary schools
summary: The resolution was moved by JUI-F MPA Shahida Rauf, who said teaching basic Arabic would help students understand commonly used Quranic words and their meanings, enabling them to develop a better understanding of the Holy Quran from an early age.
The resolution called for a simple, standardised and grade-wise curriculum covering basic Arabic vocabulary, grammar and commonly used Quranic expressions.
Following the discussion, the Assembly unanimously approved the resolution, recommending the introduction of compulsory basic Arabic education in government primary schools throughout Balochistan.

stories.title: Act now on El Nino or pay double later, UNDP chief warns
summary: This exceptionally strong cycle has already battered economies worldwide. “Not acting is the most expensive climate policy that you could have,” De Croo warned, urging major players such as the International Monetary Fund to help vulnerable developing nations mitigate the damage.

Developing countries want more financial support from wealthier nations historically responsible for global warming, though De Croo acknowledged rich governments face heavy debt burdens and war costs.

While De Croo pressed for immediate adaptation investments and policy reforms to lower capital costs across 47 partner nations, questions over long-term global climate leadership also surfaced on the sidelines of the Antalya summit.

stories.title: COP31 must deliver climate justice, not empty pledges, says Sherry
summary: As a close friend and longstanding partner, Turkiye understands the devastating human and economic costs of climate disasters.

Global fossil fuel subsidies are estimated at approximately $7 trillion. “This is an extraordinary misallocation of resources at a time when countries on the climate frontlines are struggling to finance basic adaptation, resilience and recovery.
The question is not whether the world has the resources, but whether it has the political will to redirect them,” Senator Rehman said.

stories.title: Yemeni govt forces fortify defences in Aden
summary: ABU DHABI: Yemen’s internationally recognised government is fortifying positions on the outskirts of Aden province, home to their de facto capital, as their Houthi foes seize hilltops overlooking the area, military officials told AFP.
The Houthis are now advancing east, consolidating their gains near the Red Sea while also moving closer to the Gulf of Aden.

The third military sou­rce, a field officer on the ground, said the Hou­this were advancing east of the strait towards the Gulf of Aden coast after taking large parts of Al-Madaribah wal Ara district.

stories.title: Situationer: ‘Time flies’ after judicial hierarchy rewritten
summary: IT HAS been a year since the creation of the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), and in the words of its top judge, the time “passed so swiftly that the passage of time had scarcely been felt”.
Created under the controversial 27th Constitutional Amendment, the FCC came into being on Nov 13, 2025, and Justice Aminuddin was sworn in as the inaugural chief justice the next day.
However, the frosty relations between the SC and FCC were evident from the start, as no one from the Supreme Court — not even CJP Yahya Afridi — turned up for the swearing-in ceremony.

stories.title: Turkiye, Qatar sign defence agreement: Turkish presidency
summary: Turkiye and Qatar signed a defence agreement on Friday that President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said would further strengthen ties between the regional allies, his office said.
In August, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement in Makkah, bringing together the Sunni Muslim US allies at a time of conflict across the region.

Turkiye’s parliament ratified the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement last week, clearing the way for Ankara to send military support to Saudi Arabia, which has been struggling to fend off attacks by Yemen’s Houthis.

stories.title: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' as outage triggers global chaos
summary: Microsoft on Friday apologized for a global outage that disrupted public services and businesses around the world, as it reported a “broad recovery” for Outlook email and other services.

Microsoft 365 is the company’s cloud-based subscription service that includes popular applications such as Outlook and Teams. ‘Improvements’ in North America, Europe Microsoft said earlier that it was seeing “improvements” for Outlook email and other services.
Microsoft last month reported an outage of its Azure cloud platform that impacted the tech giant’s suite of productivity software, and a range of industries worldwide.

stories.title: President House says matters related to provinces did not come under discussion during Zardari, Naqvi meeting
summary: The President House on Friday refuted media reports about yesterday’s meeting between President Asif Ali Zardari and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, saying that discussions focused on national security and regional situation.
The clarification comes after several media reports emerged claiming that Naqvi and the president had discussed the formation of new provinces during a meeting in Nawabshah on Thursday night.

Meanwhile, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari has called for a “full stop” on the debate surrounding new provinces and also a “political reset”, wherein all political parties must unite for the sake of the country rather than indulge in “unnecessary debates”.

stories.title: Nvidia approached Arm CEO Haas to succeed Huang, FT reports
summary: Nvidia’s board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang, the Financial Times reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

US Treasury chief blames Commerce Dept for failure in Nvidia scandal Meanwhile, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Friday blamed the Commerce Department for failing to blacklist Megaspeed, the Singapore company at the centre of the Nvidia scandal.
Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital affair in a November 8 letter to Nvidia employees that did not name the woman involved and resigned his position on Thursday.

stories.title: Pakistan set to host FIH Hockey Nations Cup in Lahore next year
summary: Pakistan will host a major International Hockey Federation (FIH) event after a gap of 24 years, with the fifth edition of the FIH Hockey Men’s Nations Cup scheduled to be held in Lahore from February 19 to 28, 2027.
Addressing the ceremony, Ikram described the Nations Cup as a major international hockey event and termed its return to Pakistan a significant moment for the country and the sport.

The 10-day competition will bring together teams from five continents, offering Pakistan an opportunity to demonstrate its capacity to host major international sporting events while giving the national side a chance to return to the elite level of international hockey.

stories.title: Govt to levy up to 10% ADL on ICE vehicles
summary: PHEVs with a minimum battery range of 50km in a single charge, as per NEV Policy 2025-30, will attract 9% sales tax; REEVs using a generator to charge batteries and having an external source of charging will attract 6%; and pure BEVs will attract 1%.
Lowering sales tax and other taxes alone will not sufficiently reduce NEV prices, so ADL will be imposed on ICE vehicles only.
The proposed sales tax rate will be the same on imported and locally manufactured motor vehicles, and the ADL rate on imported and locally manufactured ICE vehicles will also be the same.

stories.title: MSC eyes Pakistan maritime investment
summary: Global shipping giant Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC) has expressed interest in exploring investment opportunities in Pakistan following a high-level meeting in Geneva.

Federal Minister for Board of Investment Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh met with MSC Chief Executive Officer Soren Toft at the company's headquarters to discuss potential investment opportunities and avenues for expanding MSC's engagement with Pakistan, a statement said on Friday.
The minister invited an MSC delegation to visit Pakistan to explore cooperation.

stories.title: Transsion eyes local phone parts production
summary: Chinese conglomerate Transsion Holdings has outlined plans to expand its investment in Pakistan and move beyond assembly into component manufacturing, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb was told during a meeting with its Founder and Chairman George Zhu on Friday.
Separately, Advisor to the Prime Minister for Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan met a Shenzhen Transsion delegation to discuss investment and export promotion in electronics.

Khan invited Chinese firms to invest, saying "Now is the right time to invest in Pakistan," while Transsion representatives expressed interest in expanding their local manufacturing footprint and pursuing deeper localisation.

stories.title: PSX recovers 500 points on gold discovery
summary: On the contribution front, MARI, LUCK, PPL, PSEL and FATIMA emerged as the leading positive contributors, collectively adding approximately 722 points to the benchmark index and providing substantial support to the market's overall performance.
Meanwhile, market participation remained robust, with total traded volume reaching approximately 1,042 million shares, while traded value stood at around Rs31 billion.
KTrade stated that the KSE-100 index closed at 177,873 points, gaining 500 points (+0.28% DoD), while total traded volume stood at 195 million shares.

stories.title: Govt meets IMF fiscal conditions
summary: The four provinces collectively generated a cash surplus of Rs599 billion, exceeding the IMF target by Rs83 billion.
The non-tax revenues of the five governments amounted to Rs2.6 trillion, Rs430 billion, or 14%, less than in the last fiscal year.
On the expenditure side, the federal government spent a total of Rs3.1 trillion during the first three months, with only Rs81 billion in development expenditures.

stories.title: Mossad chief visits Washington as Israel presses Trump to resume Iran war: Report
summary: The director of Israel’s Mossad intelligence agency was in Washington on Friday for talks with senior Trump administration officials about the war with Iran, Axios reported, citing three sources familiar with the matter.
Trump said Thursday he could use military force against Iran "right now" if US allies or ships were threatened.
We’re doing very well with it right now." BREAKING: TRUMP ON IRAN: REPORTER: Would you hesitate to use military force against Iran?

stories.title: Faxes, phones and Bluetooth: Microsoft outage forces businesses to find fixes
summary: Old-school technology including telephones, faxes and Bluetooth limited the damage for some people on Friday as a worldwide outage of Microsoft’s Outlook left millions without email.
Microsoft, which says on its website that more than 430 million people use its 365 services, blamed server problems and said it was not aware of any malicious activity.
Fax machines return in Taipei In Taiwan, the outage disrupted fund management at securities firms, life insurers and investment trust companies, people familiar with the situation said.

stories.title: Barrick Mining expresses interest in mineral processing industries in Karachi, Gwadar
summary: It added that the prime minister also expressed a desire to draw on Barrick’s expertise and experience to develop Pakistan’s mineral sector beyond Reko Diq.

According to a statement by the PMO, designating Pakistan a “priority destination” for mineral investment reflects growing confidence among global investors in the country mineral potential and investment climate.

Furthermore, per the statement, the PM said the exchange of MoUs at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum was a “welcome” development. “Creating a conducive environment for investment in the minerals sector is among the government’s priorities.

stories.title: COP has a guest-list problem
summary: Moved by her experience, Jamali decided to apply for participation in the 27th edition of United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) COP, scheduled to be held in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt in November that year.

Durlabh Ashok, founding director of Climate Forward Pakistan (CFP), a leading youth-led climate organisation that sends delegations to COP every year, says the organisation offers limited financial assistance to its delegates.
He was selected to attend COP30 through Climate Forward Pakistan (CFP), however, he was required to submit $2,200 (approximately PKR 620,448 at the time) for the trip.

stories.title: Nvidia fallout throws spotlight on Southeast Asia’s AI boom
summary: Southeast Asia’s chip and data centre industries expect greater scrutiny after news of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy put the spotlight on Singapore and Malaysia, executives and analysts said.

The alleged spy, Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, was an executive at a cloud computing firm in Singapore called Megaspeed that has subsidiaries in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Australia and the US.

Gary Goh, CEO of Malaysia-based data centre consultancy Sprint DC, likened the current situation to a “post-DeepSeek moment”. “Once the new rules are out, there will be a lot more restrictions for countries like Malaysia.

stories.title: Pakistan aiming to become competitive destination for long-term investment, CDF Munir tells minerals moot
summary: As the two-day event opened on Thursday, Pakistan showcased its vast mineral resources, ranging from coal and salt to gold and critical minerals, to attract international investment, promising predictable, investor-friendly policies, institutional support and security.
PM expresses hope for Pakistan’s economy Addressing the same event, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed the hope that Pakistan could become the world’s sixth-largest economy “earlier than 2050”.

Regarding Pakistan’s efforts to meet investor expectations, PM Shehbaz highlighted that the country was simplifying procedures, “eliminating red tape, cutting inordinate delays and ensuring complete transparency in awarding licences and contracts”.

stories.title: Judges close part of ICC Afghanistan investigations that could look at US troops
summary: Judges at the International Criminal Court have issued a decision to formally close part of the prosecutor's investigations into Afghanistan that previously ​looked at alleged crimes by US troops and to focus only ‌on actions of the Taliban since 2021, court documents show.

The decision by the chamber formally closes not only the line of inquiry into alleged crimes by US troops, which ​had already lain dormant since 2021, but also a probe into the ​Islamic State Khorasan (ISIS-K) militia.
Judges said they had decided to close part of ​the case because prosecutors ​had not shown ⁠they would be able to effectively investigate allegations in Afghanistan apart from the Taliban probe.

stories.title: Europe's security cannot be part of Ukraine peace talks, EU leaders say
summary: European Union (EU) leaders said on Friday that Europe's security structure should not be a subject for Ukraine-Russia peace negotiations, ‌but they did not answer the question of who should speak for Europe in any future talks.

Europe prioritises ceasefire in Russia-Ukraine War EU foreign policy ​chief Kaja Kallas said Russian calls for discussions about Europe's security architecture risked diverting attention from the need for a ceasefire.

During a meeting on Thursday, leaders from Poland, the Baltics and Nordic states warned against brainstorming with the ‌US or ⁠Russia about Europe’s security architecture, according to a European diplomat and a European official.

stories.title: Pakistan, bad weather hold Sri Lanka to draw in first Test
summary: Led by Saud Shakeel and aided by bad weather, Pakistan foiled Sri Lanka’s bid for victory as the first Test ended in a draw on the fifth and final day in Rawalpindi on Friday.
Sri Lanka had sniffed victory with four wickets in the first session, with Pakistan 151-5 at lunch and a lead of 139.
Earlier, Sri Lanka struck with the first ball of the day when Kumara dismissed Azan Awais for 22 at Pakistan’s overnight total of 57.

stories.title: Petrol drops by Rs2, diesel remains unchanged till Nov 16
summary: The federal government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Rs2 while keeping the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) unchanged till November 16.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs330 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs360 per litre from November 14 to November 16.
The revision comes a day after the government reduced the prices of petrol and HSD by Rs3 and Rs4 per litre, respectively, for November 13.

stories.title: Turkiye and Qatar sign mutual defence agreement, Turkish presidency says
summary: Turkiye and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement on Friday, ​the office of President Tayyip Erdogan said, as ‌the Turkish leader met the Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani in Istanbul.
"President Erdogan stated that the Mutual Defence Agreement ‌signed ⁠today by Turkiye and Qatar would add another dimension to our brotherhood," it added.
In August, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement in Mecca, bringing together ​the Sunni ​Muslim US allies ⁠at a time of conflict across the region.

stories.title: UN chief urges drastic emissions cuts as COP31 wrestles with fossil fuels
summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Friday called for an "immediate and drastic reduction" in greenhouse gas emissions, as divisions over fossil fuels ​dominated the first week of COP31 climate talks in Turkiye.

Big fossil fuel producers and consumers at the talks are resisting any deal that would specify firm ‌new targets or a shift away from oil, gas and coal, observers said as the first week of talks drew to a close.

The world’s biggest oil consumer, the United States, meanwhile, has skipped the talks for the second year in a row under President Donald Trump, who has called global warming a ​hoax and promoted continued use of fossil fuels.

stories.title: North Korean hackers stole $400m using fake video calls: FBI
summary: North Korea’s state-backed hackers stole more than $400 million using a “highly effective social engineering scheme” involving identity theft and AI-powered fake video calls, the FBI said on Thursday.
The FBI said that, aside from the Binance hack, North Koreans have “aggressively [targeted] individuals in the cryptocurrency and Web3 sectors through deceptive social engineering tactics”.
FaceStealer hackers pretend to be someone known to the victim to lure them to a video meeting, using AI-powered deepfake video to gain trust.

stories.title: Colette Kress, the CFO who challenged Huang's bets, is Nvidia's interim CEO
summary: Colette Kress spent years as the one Nvidia executive willing to check CEO Jensen Huang’s enormous, ​often risky ambitions.
Questions are also swirling about how much Kress knew about Nvidia's chip sales and Huang's affairs.
A fifth source said Kress knew about his relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, ​who reported to him.

stories.title: Short-term inflation clocks in at 11.21pc
summary: Short-term inflation has remained in the double digits for several consecutive weeks, largely on the back of persistent increases in petroleum and diesel prices.
The Sensitive Price Index (SPI), which tracks short-term inflation, slightly declined by 0.46pc week-on-week, reflecting price fluctuations in both food and non-food items.

The items that recorded the highest price increases over the previous week included tomatoes (12.06pc), eggs (5.98pc), potatoes (2.42pc), garlic (1.76pc), chicken (1.32pc), firewood (1.10pc), wheat flour (0.94pc), pulse masoor (0.64pc), beef (0.47pc), and LPG (0.30pc).

stories.title: No provincial matters discussed at Zardari-Naqvi meeting in Nawabshah: President House
summary: The President’s House on Friday issued a clarification regarding a meeting between President Asif Ali Zardari and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, rejecting media reports suggesting that provincial matters had come under discussion.

Among them was PML-N leader and Prime Minister's aide Rana Sanaullah, who questioned how Naqvi could criticise the political system after rising to the office of interior minister through the same system in just three and a half years.
Also Read: PML-N's Asif backs twelve new provinces On September 4, the Sindh Assembly passed a resolution rejecting attempts to divide the province or create new administrative units.

stories.title: Amazon’s plan to own the world’s product data and fight AI shopping agents
summary: Called World Product Graph, the initiative seeks to hoover up data on virtually every item for sale on Earth, whether Amazon stocks it or not, ​according to an internal document reviewed by Reuters, and to people familiar with the matter.
Amazon has already signed up Coca-Cola and Bayer, among others, to contribute product data, the document says.
Yet Amazon executives have grown wary of AI shopping agents that may ​send customer traffic to other sites that have greater or more complete data, according to people familiar with the matter.

stories.title: Legislature cannot be 'bypassed', minister says on question of referendum on new provinces
summary: Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said on Friday that Parliament and the provincial assemblies could not be "bypassed or negated" on the question of making new provinces through a referendum to determine the public will.

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah rejected Naqvi’s assessment that the governance system had collapsed and called the proposal outdated, warning that no bloodshed would be allowed over the creation of new provinces.

Also Read: PTI's Barrister Gohar warns against dividing provinces without broad public consensus Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, while accepting that Sindh had the right to take its own position, also said a final decision would have to emerge through consensus.

stories.title: ECP warns of orders if PMO fails to submit request for cantonment polls
summary: The commission issued the direction in an order passed on November 10 by a five-member bench headed by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja, while hearing a case regarding the delay in holding local government elections in 42 cantonment boards across the country.
During the meeting, the commission directed the defence ministry to initiate the requisite summary for obtaining the federal government’s written request and forward it to the ECP.

It further observed that Articles 140-A and 219(d) of the Constitution, read with Section 219 of the Elections Act, 2017, placed an obligation on the ECP to hold local government elections in the provinces, Islamabad Capital Territory and cantonment boards.

stories.title: Islamabad to become country's first fully cashless city by year-end
summary: ISLAMABAD: The government has decided to make the federal capital the country’s first fully cashless city, setting Dec 31 as the deadline for the transition.

The decision was taken at an important meeting on the Cashless Capital project chaired by State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudry, in Islamabad on Friday, according to an official statement by the Ministry of Interior on X.
Representatives of the banking sector appreciated the government’s Cashless Islamabad initiative and assured full cooperation for its success, it added.

stories.title: Copper, gold deposits identified at eight sites in Balochistan’s Chagai district: mining company
summary: ISLAMABAD: Mining company National Resources Limited (NRL) on Friday announced that it had identified copper and gold deposits at eight sites in Balochistan’s Chagai district, following nearly 25,000 metres of drilling that yielded encouraging results.

Tabba reaffirmed NRL’s previously announced commitment of $100 million to mineral exploration in Pakistan and invited domestic and international investors and service providers to explore emerging opportunities.
The company’s technical workforce is almost entirely local, supporting its ambition to build domestic expertise that could also contribute to international exploration projects.

stories.title: Delhi overtakes Lahore as world's most polluted major city as air quality deteriorates
summary: India’s capital, Delhi, overtook Lahore to become the world’s most polluted city on Friday, with air quality reaching hazardous levels and visibility dropping as smog blanketed the city of 20 million people.

Earlier, Delhi’s air quality index (AQI) stood at 334, categorised as “hazardous”, making it the most polluted major city globally, according to Swiss air quality monitoring group IQAir, which measures pollution levels based on the concentration of pollutants.

The spokesperson said comparative data for the period between Jan 1 and Nov 10 this year showed a “substantial increase” in inspections, regulatory action and financial penalties against polluting industries and brick kilns compared to the corresponding period last year.
